products.name: Uber
products.key_insight: Uber is a case study in dual-sided behavioral design: the company applies behavioral science to both riders (friction elimination, surge anchoring) and drivers (gamification, loss aversion goals). The ethical tension is asymmetric — riders benefit from reduced friction, but drivers are nudged to work longer hours in ways that may not serve their interests. Uber's behavioral design works precisely because it's invisible: users don't know they're being nudged, and drivers don't realize the earnings goal is an anchor, not a recommendation.
